title: Grade 3 Science — Fri, Jun 27
description: Plants Around Us — Day 5 of 5: Mixed review
subject: science

questions.question: Which part of a plant makes food using sunlight?
questions.explanation: Leaves make food through photosynthesis using sunlight, water and carbon dioxide.

questions.question: A carrot plant has one thick main root that stores food. This is a:
questions.explanation: Carrot has a taproot — the edible part IS the thick taproot that stores nutrients.

questions.question: Which dispersal method does a dandelion seed use?
questions.explanation: Dandelion seeds have fluffy, hair-like structures (pappus) that allow the wind to carry them far away — wind dispersal.

questions.question: Rice has many thin roots spreading from the base. This is a ___ root.
questions.explanation: Rice has fibrous roots — a mass of thin, similar-sized roots spreading from the stem base.

questions.question: Leaves have two types of venation. The net-like pattern is called:
questions.explanation: Reticulate (net-like) venation has veins branching in a net pattern. Most trees and flowering plants (mango, rose) show reticulate venation.

questions.question: Identify the correct match:
questions.explanation: Banyan tree has a woody stem — hard and durable. Grass and wheat have fibrous roots; mango has a taproot; herbaceous stems are soft (sunflower, tomato).

questions.question: A pod of touch-me-not (Mimosa) bursts open and scatters its seeds. This is:
questions.explanation: Touch-me-not (Mimosa) and peas use explosive dispersal — the dried pod bursts and flings seeds outward.

questions.question: Which of the following is a function of ROOTS?
options: Absorb water and minerals from soil
questions.explanation: Roots absorb water and dissolved minerals from the soil and anchor the plant. Making food is done by leaves; attracting pollinators is done by flowers.

questions.question: Why are mango fruits bright yellow and sweet when ripe?
options: To protect the seeds from heat
To attract animals so they eat the fruit and disperse the seeds
Yellow colour means the seed is dead
questions.explanation: Bright colour and sweetness attract fruit-eating animals (birds, monkeys). They eat the fruit and deposit the seed elsewhere — animal seed dispersal.

questions.question: Which grass-related plant has parallel venation?
questions.explanation: Wheat is a monocot grass plant with parallel venation. Mango, peepal and rose are dicots with reticulate venation.

questions.question: What does a stem do for a plant? (Choose the MOST COMPLETE answer)
options: Transports water and minerals from roots to leaves, and food from leaves to all parts; supports the plant structure
questions.explanation: The stem's main jobs: (1) structural support, (2) transport of water/minerals upward (via xylem), (3) transport of food downward (via phloem).

questions.question: A student says 'seeds need sunlight to germinate'. Is this correct?
options: Yes, sunlight is the most important factor
No — seeds need water, warmth and oxygen for germination; sunlight is needed only AFTER sprouting
Yes, but only big seeds need sunlight
Partly correct — some seeds need light, most don't need anything
questions.explanation: Germination does NOT require sunlight. Seeds germinate underground (no light). They need water (activates enzymes), warmth (provides energy), and oxygen (for respiration). Sunlight is needed only after the seedling emerges.

questions.question: Compare fibrous and taproot systems: which helps the plant survive drought better and why?
options: Fibrous — it covers more soil area
Taproot — it reaches deeper water sources that remain available even when topsoil dries up
questions.explanation: Taproot grows deep, reaching underground water even when the surface soil is dry — giving drought resistance. Fibrous roots are shallow and would dry out sooner in a drought.

questions.question: A plant community is disturbed — all plants with fibrous roots are removed. What might happen to the soil?
options: Topsoil loses its binding — increased erosion by wind and water, loss of fertile topsoil
questions.explanation: Fibrous root mats bind topsoil. Remove fibrous-rooted plants (grasses) and the topsoil has nothing holding it together — wind and rain carry it away (erosion), degrading the land.

questions.question: Describe the full journey of a mango seed from the fruit to growing into a new plant.
options: Seed falls, lands in water, floats away, germinates
Mango ripens and falls → animal eats fruit → seed deposited in droppings → seeds germinate with water and warmth → seedling grows into a new mango tree
Wind carries the seed → seed lands far away → grows
Seed is planted by a farmer → waters it → grows with sunlight
questions.explanation: Mango uses animal dispersal: ripe fruit attracts animals → animal eats fruit → seed passes through digestive system → deposited with droppings in a new location → with water and warmth, the seed germinates → new mango tree grows.
